name: Casuarina Coast Asmat
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Newguineaworld (T. Usher), page 'Casuarina Coast Asmat' (last modified 2024-06-25)
the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Asmat' (keyed to ISO asc 'Asmat, Casuarina Coast'), passage 618 = Voorhoeve 1965:25-26
sources.note: StressTyp2's Asmat entry is mis-keyed to asc: its only descriptive passage is Voorhoeve 1965 on the Flamingo Bay (Kawenak) dialect = Central Asmat [cent2117], already carried in our catalog under cent2117. Not evidence for casu1237.

sources.citation: Drabbe, P. 1963. Drie Asmat-dialecten. Verhandelingen KITLV 42. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. (sec. 1 p. 1; sec. 9 Aantekening p. 13; Woordenlijst van Keenakap, Kaünak en Kaweinag pp. 212-233)
sources.note: Stress rule (p. 13: final in disyllables, initial in trisyllables; deviating stress marks a compound) is given for Kawenak/Keenok/Keenakap = Central/Yaosakor Asmat only. Drabbe says explicitly (p. 1) he could not study the Casuarina Coast dialect (Kawejnag); it appears only as a 377-item wordlist filled in by Father A. v.d. Wouw, with no prosodic notes.

sources.citation: Usher, T. & Suter, E. 2020. The Asmat-Muli languages of Southwestern New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 38: 148-175.
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory; nothing on stress. p. 154 states only Central Asmat is well described, Citak has Kruidhof 1979, and all other Asmat lects (incl. Casuarina Coast) rest on Drabbe 1963 and Voorhoeve 1980 wordlists.

sources.citation: Pawley, A. & Hammarström, H. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In B. Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Documentation index lists Casuarina Coast Asmat [asc] as 'wordlist: Drabbe 1963b, Voorhoeve 1980' only; prosody paragraph says most Asmat-Kamoro languages lack tonal prosody (Kamoro and Citak tonal). Nothing on CC stress.
sources.venue: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area

sources.citation: de Antoni, Alexander. 2009. Einbaum nach Drüben: In mythische Erzählungen und kosmologische Vorstellungen der Asmat eingeschriebene Strukturen der sozialen Ordnung. PhD, Universität Wien. 280 pp.
sources.note: Only modern work based on fieldwork in the Kaweinag (CC) area; ethnographic, but may contain an orthography/pronunciation note. Low expectation.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1980. The Asmat languages of Irian Jaya. Pacific Linguistics B-64. Canberra: ANU. (ch. 6 'Casuarina Coast Asmat' pp. 39-42, sec. 6.2 'Phonology and Lexicon' p. 41; sec. 3.1.2.3 p. 22; sec. 7.2 p. 43)
sources.note: For CC only an impressionistic phoneme inventory from taped wordlists; notes 'quite distinctive pitch patterns' but cannot say whether intonational or tonal; sec. 7.2 states stress and pitch have only been studied in the KW dialect of Central Asmat and in Citak. No stress-placement statement for Casuarina Coast Asmat.

sources.citation: Balai Bahasa Papua / Badan Bahasa reports on 'bahasa Asmat Safan' or 'Asmat Pantai Kasuari' (cf. Budiono 2021, Identifikasi dan Penentuan Status Bahasa di Kabupaten Asmat, Prosiding KIMLI, 359-364, which lists 'Asmat Safan')
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Indonesian government language-mapping work sometimes includes a fonologi section with a tekanan (stress) remark; repositori.kemdikbud.go.

sources.citation: Roesler, Cal. 1972. The phonology of the Ajam dialect of Asmat. MA thesis, Hartford Seminary Foundation, 64 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Not CC (Ajam = Central Asmat, cns) but the only dedicated Asmat phonology; Voorhoeve 1980:22 reports Roesler analyses two tones. Would inform the family-level picture, not casu1237 itself.
sources.venue: MA thesis, Hartford Seminary Foundation, 64 pp
